## Overview

This Adyen online-payments guide describes how to pre-authorize, adjust and manually capture card payments, plus the distinct asynchronous adjustment path for Klarna. It is a procedural website snapshot collected on 2026-09-15; the exact request fields, response examples and SDK snippets remain in the pinned raw page.

The snapshot does not prove current availability, issuer approval, Merchant Category Code eligibility, account configuration, authorization extension, adjustment success or capture success.

## Key takeaways

- The standard card sequence begins with a pre-authorization, uses the original payment PSP reference for later amount-update and capture requests, and manually captures after the final intended adjustment. The merchant must decide when to use the flow and calculate each new amount. When Adyen Support has enabled multiple partial captures, the documented card sequence can instead partially capture and then adjust the authorized amount; the issuer determines how many partial captures are possible and may flag multiple partial captures as fraud risk, causing capture failure.
- A card amount update supplies the new total authorized amount, not merely the increment. Asynchronous adjustment returns a received request state and requires an `AUTHORISATION_ADJUSTMENT` webhook for the result. Synchronous card adjustment requires account enablement and the latest `adjustAuthorisationData` blob for each successive update.
- Capture remains asynchronous and must be confirmed from webhook events. Completing a capture request or receiving its immediate response does not establish that funds were captured.
- For the card flow, adjustment support is limited by payment method, MCC, issuer decision and Adyen acquisition; authorization validity depends on the card scheme. Card adjustment requests cannot use a zero value and are capped at 50 per payment.
- For the card flow, authorization extension uses an amount update equal to the current authorized balance. Adyen recommends the asynchronous path for card extension because Visa and Discover only support asynchronous extension adjustments; issuer refusal ends the initially authorized payment, while a Mastercard amount adjustment also extends validity. The snapshot does not state that these card extension rules or the 50-adjustment cap govern Klarna.
- Klarna is pre-authorized by default and supports only asynchronous authorization adjustment. Its authorization can be adjusted while it has not been cancelled, expired or fully captured; after a partial capture the adjusted total cannot be below the amount already captured. Increasing the authorization triggers another risk assessment or credit lookup; rejection requires a new order while the original authorization remains valid.

## Material boundaries

> [!warning] Eligibility and issuer outcome
> The guide limits authorization adjustment to supported payment methods and MCCs, payments acquired by Adyen, and issuer acceptance. Documentation of the flow is not proof that a particular merchant, payment or issuer supports it.

> [!warning] Webhook-authoritative outcomes
> Use the required webhook events to determine asynchronous adjustment and capture outcomes. Immediate request acceptance or a `received` response is not final authorization or capture proof.

> [!warning] Final-capture sequencing and enabled partial captures
> For the normal final-capture sequence, finish all intended adjustments before capture and do not infer adjustability from an unresolved asynchronous capture. A separate card exception exists when Adyen Support has enabled multiple partial captures: the guide permits partial capture followed by authorization adjustment, but the issuer controls how many partial captures are possible and may reject a capture after treating the pattern as fraud risk.

quotes.text: This page explains how to adjust [authorizations](/get-started-with-adyen/adyen-glossary/#authorization?target=_blank) for card payments, and for [Klarna](/payment-methods/klarna) payments.
You will rely on webhook events to know whether the capture succeeds. If you use asynchronous authorization adjustment, you will also rely on webhook events for the authorization adjustment result.
You can only adjust authorizations for payments acquired by Adyen.

You can make a maximum of 50 adjustments to the pre-authorized amount on a single payment transaction. After that, all subsequent requests to adjust the pre-authorized amount will be declined. You will still be able to capture the transaction up to the last successfully pre-authorized amount.

## Overview

Adyen authorization adjustment is an online-payments flow for changing the reserved amount on an eligible pre-authorized card or Klarna payment before final capture. It applies only to supported payment methods and Merchant Category Codes, depends on issuer acceptance, and is limited to payments acquired by Adyen.

## Card lifecycle

In the standard card sequence, the merchant pre-authorizes the payment, submits amount updates against the original payment PSP reference, and manually captures after the final intended adjustment. Asynchronous adjustment and capture outcomes are established through webhook events; a request response with a received state is not final outcome evidence. Synchronous card adjustment requires account enablement and successive use of the latest `adjustAuthorisationData` blob.

When Adyen Support has enabled multiple partial captures, a documented card exception permits a partial capture followed by an adjustment of the authorized amount. The issuer determines how many partial captures are possible and can flag multiple partial captures as fraud risk, causing capture failure. This exception does not make an unresolved asynchronous final capture evidence that another adjustment is safe.

## Card constraints and extension

- Each card update expresses the new total authorized amount rather than only the increment.
- Card adjustments cannot use a zero value, and the card-flow section permits at most 50 adjustments per payment; later adjustment requests are declined while capture remains possible up to the last successfully authorized amount.
- Card authorization validity depends on the card scheme. Extension uses an amount update equal to the current authorized balance and remains issuer-dependent. Visa and Discover support only asynchronous extension adjustments, while a Mastercard amount adjustment also extends validity.
- For normal final capture, merchants must finish all intended adjustments before starting capture and use webhook outcomes as the authoritative result; the Support-enabled multiple-partial-capture exception remains separately qualified above.

These limits and scheme-specific extension statements are documented in the card-flow section; the snapshot does not state that they apply to Klarna.

## Klarna path

Klarna is pre-authorized by default and supports only asynchronous authorization adjustment. An authorization can be adjusted while it has not been cancelled, expired or fully captured. After a partial capture, the adjusted amount cannot be below the already captured amount. Increasing the amount triggers another risk assessment or credit lookup; if that rejects the transaction, the customer must place a new order while the original authorization remains valid.
